title: Customer reference program launch (case studies + reference calls) — scope, metrics, and operating model
creator: Camila Reyes
description:
Goal
Launch a structured customer reference + case study program to support Redwood’s PLG→sales-assisted motion. We need 3–5 design partners who will (1) approve a public case study (web + PDF) and (2) participate in scheduled reference calls for qualified prospects.

Why now
Sales is consistently asked for proof of production outcomes (latency, cost/token, reliability, deployment flexibility) and peer validation for Dedicated + Private. Today references are ad-hoc, scheduling is manual, and claims language varies by AE. This initiative creates a repeatable, legally-safe operating model + a small initial set of high-quality public stories.

In scope
1) Program definition + governance
- Eligibility criteria for reference customers (usage stability, champion, supportability, willingness, legal constraints)
- Roles/responsibilities across Marketing/Sales/CS/SE/Legal
- Routing + SLA for reference call requests (who approves, who schedules, how fast)
- Governance for claims/metrics language and security review

2) Case study production (3–5)
- Standard template + style guide, interview plan, metrics checklist
- Validation notes for measurable outcomes (measurement window, baselines, caveats)
- Legal/comms approvals (logo/quote releases; NDA considerations)
- Publishing workflow (web + PDF), plus internal enablement roll-out

3) Reference call operations
- Intake form, qualification checklist, routing rules
- Customer prep one-pager + prospect prep (context, agenda, do/don’t)
- Scheduling process + cadence guardrails for customers
- Feedback loop after each call (what landed, what to improve)

Out of scope
- Brand campaign / paid media
- Major website redesign beyond a case-studies section update
- Product changes not required to support claims (minor docs updates allowed)

Proposed timeline (8–10 weeks)
Weeks 1–2: Templates, legal workflow, target list, outreach plan, tracking in HubSpot
Weeks 3–5: Recruitment + kickoff interviews; validate metrics + architecture details
Weeks 6–8: Drafts → internal review → customer review/redlines → design + publishing
Weeks 9–10: Reference call program live + enablement rollout + retro

Deliverables
A) Reference program playbook (internal)
- Eligibility criteria + “reference readiness” rubric
- Intake → qualification → scheduling → prep → post-call follow-up workflow
- Routing rules (AE owner, CS approval, SE support) + scheduling SLA
- Governance: claims review, security review, legal sign-off, final approver list

B) Case study template pack
- Interview guide (eng + business)
- Metrics validation worksheet + acceptable phrasing examples
- Approval checklist (quote verification, logo usage, security review, final sign-off)

C) 3–5 published case studies
- Web page + PDF for each (or web-only where PDF is blocked)
- Internal “reference profile” for each customer (what topics they cover, limits)

D) Tracking + reporting
- HubSpot fields for reference readiness, approval status, spokesperson, restrictions
- Program dashboard: case studies in pipeline, reference calls completed, outcomes

E) Enablement
- Talk track + discovery prompts + objection handling snippets (security, Dedicated vs Private)
- Single source of truth for requesting references + asset links

Success metrics (target for initial launch window)
- 3 public case studies published with approved metrics + architecture detail
- 5+ completed reference calls within first 30 days of program going live
- ≥$1.5M influenced pipeline within 60 days (self-reported + HubSpot association)
- Internal SLA: 80% of reference requests scheduled within 5 business days (once approved)
- Zero instances of unapproved customer logo/quote usage; no security-sensitive disclosures in published assets

Definition of done
- Playbook published in Confluence and linked from #sales and #marketing pinned docs
- Intake form live + routing automation configured + owners trained
- Case studies section live on docs/website (ENG-4921)
- PDF template ready and used for at least 2 published stories (DES-214)
- HubSpot properties + automation live (ENG-4978) and being used by AEs/CSMs
- At least 3 customers fully executed release forms (or documented exception with Legal)

Key stakeholders / approvers
- Exec sponsor: Jordan Blake (CRO)
- Program owner: Camila Reyes (VP Marketing)
- Messaging/claims lead: Soojin Lee (Dir Product Marketing)
- CS readiness + customer coordination: Rachel Kim / Miguel Santos
- SE validation: Markus Klein / Simran Kaur
- Metrics rigor: Sana Farid / Logan Wright
- Legal: Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes
- Security claims review: Naomi Feldman

Risks + mitigations
- Legal delays: start release discussions at recruitment; provide “quotes-only / no logo” option; pre-approved claim language library.
- Metrics disputes: require measurement notes + source-of-truth dashboards; do not publish single-point benchmarks without window + workload caveats.
- Customer bandwidth: keep interviews to 45 min; draft-first approach; provide final approval checkpoint with clear delta.
- Security review sensitivity (especially Private/VPC): publish architecture at the right abstraction level; avoid identifiers (regions, IP ranges, vendor tooling specifics).

Open questions
- What is the minimum bar for a public case study vs an anonymized story? (Need Legal + Security guidance.)
- Do we allow references without public story (reference-only)? If yes, how do we tag and govern frequency?
- Pipeline influence attribution: confirm HubSpot association approach with RevOps (Isabelle Laurent).

comments: 2025-05-02 — Jordan Blake: Aligning on exec priority. This needs to unblock Dedicated/Private deals where we’re losing to “no proof in production.” Please keep success metrics crisp and attributable; include a retro + pipeline review date in the plan.

2025-05-06 — Rachel Kim: Strongly recommend we define a CS-controlled ‘reference readiness’ rubric. We’ve had issues when references are asked to speak during unstable rollouts. Propose: (a) 30+ days in prod, (b) identified champion + backup, (c) known limitations documented (topics to avoid), (d) incident summary reviewed.

2025-05-09 — Markus Klein: For metrics, we need repeatable measurement notes. Suggest we require: baseline window, Redwood window, traffic shape assumptions, and whether results depend on batching/caching/quantization. Otherwise we’ll get stuck in endless redlines with sophisticated customers.

2025-05-14 — Sofia Mendes: Legal note: release form must explicitly list approved quotes and whether logo can be used on website, PDF, sales decks, and marketplace listings. Also add withdrawal clause language options (30–60 day notice) for sensitive accounts.

2025-05-21 — Soojin Lee: Messaging guidance: anchor stories on ‘production economics’ (latency + cost + reliability). For Private, focus on deployment flexibility + audit logs/KMS, but avoid implying any specific compliance certification beyond what Security approves. I’ll draft a claim phrasing library for p95/throughput/cost-per-query metrics.

2025-06-07 — Camila Reyes: Status check: we have 3 customers verbally positive (Arcadia, QuantaPay, NovaDocs). Need hard gating: no publish until (1) metrics validated by SE + Sana, (2) Legal release signed, (3) Security claims review completed. Adding this as an explicit checklist in the playbook.

2025-06-20 — Isabelle Laurent: RevOps update: we can attribute ‘influenced pipeline’ by associating reference call activities to deals in HubSpot + adding a ‘Reference used’ checkbox on the deal. ENG-4978 should include property creation + required fields on close-lost notes when references are requested but not provided.

2025-07-18 — Soojin Lee: Marking as Done for launch scope. Playbook content merged into Confluence, and downstream tickets (PM-701/DES-214/ENG-4921/ENG-4978) track execution. Next step is program retro and metrics readout in 60 days (tracked separately).
